alignments.note: `כִּי` takes the protasis *When* written for it (rule 55).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
The ASV writes a word for the preposition and another for the noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits them.
The ASV writes the chain as an English possessive, so the construct noun keeps only its own word (rule 29).
The rectum is written as the English possessive standing before its head noun (rule 29).
The possessive determiner stands before the possessor's word (rules 18, 29).
Apodosis waw takes the *then* written for it (rule 14).

Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17). `עֲנָבִים` is the bare direct object of the eating, with no object marker and no preposition of its own, so the supplied *of* through which the English verb reaches that object belongs to the verb's rendering (rule 44), exactly as in *hast greedily gained of thy neighbors*; the unit is discontinuous under rule 25. Rule 33 was the competing reading, but it reaches a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative or an appositional or measure nominal, and this noun is neither.
The object noun keeps only its own English word; the partitive *of* is the verb's under rule 44.
`כְּ` takes the *at* the ASV writes for it (rule 11).
`נֶפֶשׁ` rendered *pleasure*.
Emphatic possessive *thine own* belongs whole to the suffix, headed on the pronoun (rule 18).
`שֹׂבַע` rendered *fill*.
Suffix rendered by the possessive *thy* (rule 18).
Waw rendered *but* (rule 14).
Negative with its own *not*.
Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative (rules 17, 25).
Supplied object with no object morpheme in the clause; it does not join the verb merely by standing beside its rendering (rules 44, 30).
`אֶל` rendered *in*.
Noun with its own word.
Suffix rendered by the possessive *thy* (rule 18).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied *of* in *thou mayest eat of grapes* moves from `עֲנָבִים` to the verb `אָכַלְתָּ`. Rule 33 governs a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative or an appositional or measure nominal; `עֲנָבִים` is the bare direct object of the eating, so rule 44's preposition supplied to reach the verb's own object governs, as in `תְּבַצְּעִי רֵעַיִךְ` → *hast greedily gained of thy neighbors*.
The object of *put* is unexpressed in Hebrew, so the supplied *any* is `added` (rule 44).
`כֶרֶם רֵעֶךָ` is written as an English possessive, so the construct keeps only *vineyard* and the suffix's *thy* stands before the possessor's word (rules 18, 29).
